note: Hand-edited. Keys are week|matchup_id. Facts sourced from scripts/build_matchup_facts.py; every number here was checked against it. Consolation games with nothing at stake deliberately have no entry.

1|1.headline: eejacobs peaks in Week 1 and spends the next thirteen regretting it
1|1.body: Erin dropped 157.29, the high score of the week and a full 47.7 points clear of what the field managed against projection. Derrick Henry went for 31.2 and Justin Herbert added 27.9, which is the sort of opening weekend that convinces a manager he has figured something out. He finished the season 7-21, dead last. Chris Merkel scored 150.63 — comfortably above the median, a winning number in most weeks — and got nothing out of it but a 1-1 split and a Mark Andrews line (1.75) he will be answering for at every draft from now until he dies.

1|2.headline: Nabers in Paris wins by 46 with 29 points sitting on the bench
1|2.body: Nick started C.J. Stroud (8.72) over Daniel Jones (29.48), which would be the story in almost any other matchup and here barely registers — Justin Fields put up 29.5 and the rest of the roster handled it. Jake Blackwell came in 30.4 points under par: Joe Burrow 8.82, Amon-Ra St. Brown 7.75, Kenneth Walker 3.65. File this one away. Seventeen weeks later that exact roster is holding the trophy.

1|3.headline: Two managers, two quarterbacks on the bench, one accidental win
1|3.body: Josh Allen went for 38.76 and dragged Joshin Around over the line, and that is the entire list of nice things available here. Andrew left Aaron Rodgers (25.66) on his bench to start Dak Prescott (7.82), and Xavier Worthy contributed a clean 0.00. Mitch responded by benching Quentin Johnston (24.15) to start Cam Ward (2.48). Andrew's 123.93 did not clear the league median, so he 'won' the week 1-1. Nobody involved should feel anything.

1|4.headline: Titsburg Feelers set a lineup with 1.25 points of regret in it
1|4.body: 180.74, the week's high score, and Chris's optimal lineup would have been worth exactly 1.25 more — the tightest lineup anyone set in Week 1. Emeka Egbuka (22.85) and Garrett Wilson (21.50) did the heavy lifting. Nick Merkel had the specific misfortune of scoring 134.64, clearing the median and going 1-1 on the week, while Ja'Marr Chase and A.J. Brown combined for 5.90 points. Two first-round receivers. One field goal.

1|5.headline: Show Me Your Penix leaves Penix on the bench, wins anyway
1|5.body: There is no writing around this one. Matt benched Michael Penix (26.02) — the man the team is named after — to start Sam Darnold (5.40), piled 103.33 points onto his bench, left 41.21 on the table, and won by 2.41. He was saved entirely by Jared Hayes starting Tyler Higbee, who scored 0.00, while Juwan Johnson put up 18.35 from a SirWinsAlot bench seat. Neither team beat the league median. Matt went 1-1, Jared went 0-2, and the sport was invented for exactly this.

1|6.headline: Duane gets both highlights and loses by 19
1|6.body: Patrick Mahomes (26.02) and Tyler Warren (17.15) were enough for BoKnows723, which is all Jake needed them to be. Duane actually produced the two biggest individual scores in the matchup — Lamar Jackson 29.36 and Deebo Samuel 23.10 — and still lost comfortably, because the back half of Enter the Maye-Trix was Jerome Ford (0.50), Tank Bigsby (2.00) and T.J. Hockenson (4.75) while Keenan Allen sat on the bench for 18.55. Duane went 0-2 on the week. Owning the highlight reel and losing the game is a whole personality.

2|1.headline: Erin's title defense lasts exactly one week
2|1.body: Seven days after the highest score in the league, eejacobs posted 83.14 — a 74-point faceplant and 43.8 below par, the worst showing of the week by a distance. Derrick Henry went from 31.2 to 2.3. Mitch Blackwell needed none of his own good fortune to win by 47, though he did lose Jayden Reed to a 0.00 and still had 67.9 sitting on his bench. Mitch's 130.71 didn't beat the median either, so the blowout bought him a 1-1 week. Nobody wins in i LOVE mendoza.

2|2.headline: Duane starts two quarterbacks who score identically and calls it strategy
2|2.body: Lamar Jackson 26.30, Drake Maye 26.30 — Enter the Maye-Trix got the exact same number out of both of them, which is either superb roster construction or a rounding coincidence, and Duane will be telling you it's the former. 167.75 and a 2-0 week, 22.2 above par, after opening the season 0-2. Nick Merkel got 34.5 from Ja'Marr Chase and 3.20 from Geno Smith and went home 0-2 for the second week running.

2|3.headline: BoKnows723 wins with 116 points on the bench
2|3.body: Jake put up 174.16 and left more points unused than eight teams scored all week — 116.5 on the bench, headlined by Wan'Dale Robinson, who would have added 22.1 over the 5.90 Drake London managed. Tucker Kraft's 27.9 covered it. Jake Blackwell's 152.47 was the second-highest score of the week and bought him a 1-1, because Amon-Ra St. Brown's 36.95 had to carry Joe Burrow's 7.04 on its back.

2|4.headline: Show Me Your Penix leaves 108 on the bench, and this time it costs him
2|4.body: Week 1 Matt benched a 26-point quarterback and won anyway. Week 2 he benched 108.4 points, started J.J. McCarthy for 2.82, and lost by 48 with the lowest score of his season to that point. Tua Tagovailoa was available and worth 15.8 more. Chris Bova didn't need to be good — 144.85 was 23.6 below par and missed the median, so Titsburg took the win and still went 1-1. Matt went 0-2 and has now left 208 points on his bench in two weeks.

2|5.headline: Nick Bova drops 178 with Russell Wilson watching from the bench
2|5.body: Malik Nabers 37.95, James Cook 27.0, De'Von Achane 24.7 — Nabers in Paris scored the most points anyone managed in Week 2 and it still wasn't the optimal lineup, because Justin Fields put up 3.98 in the QB slot while Russell Wilson sat there worth 30.3 more. Chris Merkel's 145.02 cleared the median and lost anyway. Mark Andrews: 1.40. That is two weeks and 3.15 total points from a starting tight end.

2|6.headline: SirWinsAlot finally wins something
2|6.body: Jared came in 0-2 and 23.8 above par is how you fix that: Jonathan Taylor 31.25, Javonte Williams 22.75, and — remarkably for this league — only 7.8 points left on the table, the cleanest lineup anyone set all week. Andrew Bova got 12.82 from Josh Allen, which is the single most disappointing sentence in this recap, and went 0-2 for it.

3|1.headline: Two 1-3 teams meet and somebody has to win
3|1.body: Breeces Peanut ButterCups took it 132.35 to 120.96, a number that didn't come close to the median, so Nick banked a 1-1 and stayed exactly as buried as he started. Zay Flowers managed 2.80 while Luther Burden sat on the bench worth 18.4 more — the swap alone would have covered the margin twice. Andrew Bova started Cade Otton, who scored 0.00, and went 0-2. Genuinely one of the games of all time.

3|2.headline: Matt starts Penix again. Penix scores 2.78.
3|2.body: Two weeks after benching Michael Penix for a 26-point afternoon, Matt put him back in the lineup and got 2.78, with Sam Darnold on the bench worth 13.9 more. There is no lineup decision available to this man that works. Hunter Henry's 32.0 out of a tight end slot kept it respectable at 127.47, but Jake Blackwell's 165.53 was 20.1 above par and never in doubt. Matt: 0-2. Show Me Your Penix is 1-5 on the season.

3|3.headline: CeeDee Lamb scores nothing and Titsburg wins anyway
3|3.body: A 0.00 from the best receiver on the roster is normally the end of a fantasy week. Chris Bova posted 155.13 regardless — Jahmyr Gibbs 25.4, Garrett Wilson 22.15, Kyren Williams 18.95 — and went 2-0 to move to 5-1. Jared Hayes got 32.8 from Jonathan Taylor and 31.12 from Caleb Williams, cleared the median, and lost. Some rosters are just deeper than yours.

3|4.headline: The best team in the league scores 105 and loses to the worst
3|4.body: BoKnows723 came in 4-0 and posted 105.58, a full 56.5 points below par — the worst performance against expectation anybody managed in 2025. Patrick Mahomes led the team with 13.16. Meanwhile 131.4 points sat on Jake's bench, including a David Montgomery worth 26.8 more than the Wan'Dale Robinson he started. Erin Jacobs won it with 116.36, which didn't beat the median either, so the upset of the season so far was a 1-1 week for the winner. Tre Tucker, incidentally, was worth 41.3 more than the man Erin started ahead of him.

3|5.headline: Mark Andrews remembers he plays football
3|5.body: After 1.75 in Week 1 and 1.40 in Week 2, Mark Andrews went for 29.35 and won Chris Merkel the game by 4.97. Three weeks, 32.5 points, and 90% of it in one afternoon — as a tight end strategy it is at least distinctive. Mitch Blackwell set the tidiest lineup of the week, leaving 0.8 on the table, scored 142.24, and lost anyway. He went 0-2 for the trouble. Setting a perfect lineup in this league is worth nothing at all.

3|6.headline: Four points decide it and Nick Bova's best receiver scores 2.55
3|6.body: Enter the Maye-Trix took it 163.66 to 159.58 on the back of Jake Ferguson's 24.2 and another Lamar Jackson day. Nabers in Paris lost by 4.08 while Malik Nabers — the man on the letterhead — put up 2.55 against an 18.92 projection, and Rico Dowdle sat on the bench worth 8.8 more. The margin was 4.08. Nick still cleared the median for a 1-1, which is the only mercy on offer here.

4|1.headline: Rivalry week, and Matt picks it to have his first good afternoon
4|1.body: 1-5 coming in, 173.87 going out, 38.2 above par and the best week anyone had against expectation. Kenny Gainwell led it with 31.61 and Romeo Doubs added 28.75 from nowhere. Duane set a near-perfect lineup — 5.7 left on the table, tidiest of the week — got 10.68 from Lamar Jackson, and lost by 27 while going 0-2. Show Me Your Penix still had 125.0 on the bench in his best week of the season, because some things are simply constitutional.

4|2.headline: BoKnows723 puts 202 on the board and it is still not his best lineup
4|2.body: The third-highest score of the 2025 season, and Jake left 60.9 on the table getting there — Justice Hill alone was worth 33.1 more than the David Montgomery who managed 1.20. Josh Jacobs 31.2, Mahomes 27.3, Jordan Love 26.28. Jared Hayes got a 34.0 out of Ashton Jeanty in rivalry week and lost by 71, which is the kind of result that makes a man question the format. Jared went 0-2.

4|3.headline: Two 5-1 teams, 361 points, and the guy on the letterhead scores 3.75
4|3.body: The best game of the week by some distance: Nabers in Paris 199.82, Titsburg Feelers 161.63, both above par, neither doing anything wrong. George Pickens went for 32.9 and Justin Fields 28.14. The comedy is that Malik Nabers — the team's actual namesake — put up 3.75, and Nick won by 38 anyway. Chris cleared the median for a 1-1 and lost his three-game streak.

4|4.headline: Nacua Matata's receivers score 99 points between them
4|4.body: Puka Nacua 34.5, Amon-Ra St. Brown 24.5, DK Metcalf 24.1 — Jake's wideouts alone outscored eight full teams this week, and the 168.31 total put him back to .500. Mitch got 22.05 from Quentin Johnston, whom he had famously benched in Week 1, and 4.52 from Cam Ward, whom he had started ahead of him. Nothing is learned in i LOVE mendoza. Mitch is 1-7.

4|5.headline: Joshin Around wins the quarterback war and nothing else
4|5.body: Dak Prescott 30.96 and Josh Allen 26.86 gave Andrew 57.82 from two quarterback slots and 11.2 from his entire running back corps, which is a distribution of resources you would struggle to design deliberately. It was enough: 138.82 beat eejacobs' 110.29 in rivalry week. It did not beat the median, so Andrew went 1-1. Erin got a 0.00 from DeMario Douglas and went 0-2 for the third time in five weeks.

4|6.headline: Merkel derby, and the wrong Merkel brings a quarterback
4|6.body: Chris got 29.4 from Matthew Stafford and 22.86 from Baker Mayfield — 52.26 from the position — and won the family game by 36. Nick's two quarterback slots produced 20.08 combined. A.J. Brown contributed 1.45, which is now a recurring feature of Breeces Peanut ButterCups rather than a bad afternoon. Nick went 0-2 and dropped to 2-6; Chris went 2-0 and sits at 6-2.

5|1.headline: SirWinsAlot gets 72 from his running backs and 3.7 from his tight end
5|1.body: Jonathan Taylor 30.85 and Javonte Williams 27.4 did essentially all of it, and Jared needed them to, because Juwan Johnson managed 3.70 and Jalen Tolbert posted a clean 0.00. 171.78 was still comfortably the better number. Nick Merkel got 29.0 from Ja'Marr Chase, 5.92 from Geno Smith, and went 0-2 again — his fourth two-loss week in five, and the season is not yet half over.

5|2.headline: i LOVE mendoza wins a game with two tight ends
5|2.body: Sam LaPorta 22.45 and David Njoku 21.2 combined for 43.65 from the tight end slots, which is not how anyone draws it up and worked completely — 174.17 and 22.2 above par, Mitch's best week of the season. Jake Bogardus started Zach Ertz, who scored 0.00, with Mason Taylor on the bench worth 20.4 more, and lost by 47. BoKnows723 went 0-2 in a week where he was still the second-best team in the league.

5|3.headline: Rico Dowdle scores 35.9 and Nick Bova barely notices
5|3.body: 191.85 for Nabers in Paris, second-highest of the week, and the remarkable part is that James Cook contributed 4.90 to it. Nick left 46.4 on the table and won by 54 regardless. Erin Jacobs got 23.45 from Kendrick Bourne — a sentence that should never have needed writing — and lost by more than fifty for the third time this season. Nick moves to 9-1.

5|4.headline: Chris Merkel starts a man named Jacory Croskey-Merritt and gets 27 points
5|4.body: That is the whole recap, really. Croskey-Merritt went 18.2 above his projection, Baker Mayfield added 26.66, and Your Team is the PITTsMAN posted 166.69 to go 2-0 and reach 8-2. Duane's problem was the SUPER_FLEX: Cooper Rush, 1.16, with Nick Chubb sitting there worth 10.9 more. Jake Ferguson's 24.65 deserved better company. Duane went 0-2.

5|5.headline: Sam Darnold repays Matt for Week 1
5|5.body: The quarterback Matt started over Michael Penix in Week 1 for 5.40 came back with 27.64, and Tua Tagovailoa added 24.74, and Show Me Your Penix won a game 155.81 to 132.80. Two 2-0 weeks in a row is not something this roster is supposed to be capable of. Andrew Bova got 30.28 from Dak Prescott, 14.6 from his entire backfield, and went 0-2. Joshin Around: 2-6.

5|6.headline: Nacua Matata scores zero points at quarterback
5|6.body: Marcus Mariota, 0.00. Not a bad afternoon — nothing at all, from the position that decides most weeks in a superflex league. Jake still managed 108.82 because Puka Nacua and Amon-Ra St. Brown are very good, and he left only 0.5 on the table, which is the cruellest detail available: this was very nearly the best lineup his roster could produce. Chris Bova's 164.89 ended it by 56. Emeka Egbuka 31.8, Kyren Williams 29.35, and Titsburg goes to 8-2.

6|1.headline: Nacua Matata scores zero at quarterback for the second week running
6|1.body: Brock Purdy: 0.00. Last week it was Marcus Mariota, also 0.00. Jake has now gone two consecutive weeks without a single point from the position, which in a superflex league is roughly equivalent to playing with ten men, and he is somehow still 5-5. Cam Skattebo's 30.25 kept it to a nine-point loss. Andrew Bova won with 117.67 that didn't clear the median, so Joshin Around took a 1-1 out of the lowest-scoring week of the season so far — the league median was 119.45, and eight teams failed to reach 120.

6|2.headline: eejacobs wins a week and immediately hides the evidence
6|2.body: Erin's 135.33 was 19.1 above par and comfortably the better team here, which after 3-7 counts as an event. He also left 44.9 on the table — Kayshon Boutte alone was worth 23.7 more than the man he started — so the celebration should be measured. Matt Bova's 119.77 squeaked over the median for a 1-1, meaning Show Me Your Penix lost the game and still banked a win. Both teams sit at 5-5 and 3-7 respectively and neither is going anywhere.

6|3.headline: Titsburg wins with 13 points from four receivers and 54 from two tight ends
6|3.body: Trey McBride 23.2, Harold Fannin 17.35 — Chris got more out of the tight end position than his entire receiving corps managed between them, which is a sentence that should end a season rather than win a game. It won the game. 119.14 was 19.2 below par and missed the median, so the 8-2 team took a 1-1. Duane started Cooper Rush, who scored minus 1.12 — the only negative number any starter posted all season — and went 0-2.

6|4.headline: SirWinsAlot gets 3.0 from the tight end slot and wins anyway
6|4.body: Jared's tight ends managed 3.00 combined, with Tyler Higbee sitting on the bench worth 14.0 more, and it never mattered — Caleb Williams, Jonathan Taylor and Trevor Lawrence carried 141.92 past a Mitch Blackwell side that got 29.95 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and 0.10 from Emari Demercado. Mitch went 0-2 again. That is seven two-loss weeks in ten for i LOVE mendoza.

6|5.headline: The 8-2 team scores 103 and loses by 93
6|5.body: Chris Merkel came in on a three-week winning streak and posted 38.1 below par with 105.8 points on his bench — Jaxson Dart alone was worth 14.3 more than the Matthew Stafford he started. Jake Bogardus, meanwhile, had the fifth-best week anyone managed against expectation all season: 196.24, a full 56.7 above par, with Mahomes 31.48, Josh Jacobs 31.0 and Drake London 30.55 all clearing thirty. The 92.91 margin is the fifth-largest of 2025. Chris went 0-2 and never really recovered the top seed.

6|6.headline: Nabers in Paris gets 94 points from two running backs
6|6.body: Rico Dowdle 32.9, De'Von Achane 30.5, Christian McCaffrey rounding out a backfield that produced 94.2 on its own. 199.98 — Nick misses 200 by two hundredths of a point, which will bother him more than any loss this season. Nick Merkel actually had a fine afternoon, 168.72 and 20.4 above par with Bijan Robinson going for 35.55, cleared the median, and lost by 31. He went 1-1 and stayed at 2-8. Some seasons are just like that.

7|1.headline: Duane snaps a three-week losing run with the best week of his season
7|1.body: 39.5 above par, which after an 0-6 stretch across three weeks is quite the reversal — Quinshon Judkins 27.4, Keenan Allen 26.65, Drake Maye 23.08. Enter the Maye-Trix goes 2-0 and climbs off the floor. Jared Hayes got 33.95 from Jonathan Taylor and 4.40 from Ashton Jeanty, missed the median by three, and went 0-2 despite scoring 132.27. The margin was 13.87.

7|2.headline: Ja'Marr Chase and A.J. Brown finally show up on the same afternoon
7|2.body: 64.7 points from the two of them, 81.1 from the receiving corps, and Breeces Peanut ButterCups snapped a three-week losing streak. Which makes it all the funnier that Geno Smith contributed 2.78 and Nick still won by 19. Erin Jacobs got 55.94 from two quarterback slots and 13.95 from his entire backfield, which is not a football team so much as a fantasy experiment, and went 0-2.

7|3.headline: BoKnows723 leaves 142 points on the bench and wins by 54
7|3.body: That is not a typo. Jake's bench outscored nine starting lineups in the league this week — 142.7 unused, the second-highest bench total of the season — and BoKnows723 still put 163.85 on the board and won comfortably. Matt Bova started Darren Waller, who scored 0.00, with Theo Johnson available and worth 17.9 more, and got precisely zero points from the tight end position. Show Me Your Penix went 0-2 and fell to 6-6.

7|4.headline: Three weeks, three zeroes at quarterback, and Jake Blackwell is still in this
7|4.body: Brock Purdy 0.00 for the second time in three weeks, Puka Nacua 0.00 alongside him, and Nacua Matata posted 81.65 — its lowest score of the season and 63.3 points short of what its own roster could have managed. Pat Freiermuth was worth 25.1 more than the man in the SUPER_FLEX. Nick Bova won by 52 with a 133.98 that did not clear the median, so the 11-1 juggernaut took a 1-1 out of a blowout. Remember which of these two teams wins the championship.

7|5.headline: Bo Nix 39.96, Oronde Gadsden 33.65, nine points in it
7|5.body: The best game of the week and one of the best of the season: Titsburg 170.67, PITTsMAN 161.60, both well above par, both getting a monster from somewhere unlikely. Chris Merkel's tight end outscored most people's entire flex, and he still lost — 100.5 on his bench, Jaxson Dart worth 21.3 more than the Baker Mayfield he started, and a 9.07 margin that any one of those decisions covers. He cleared the median for a 1-1. Chris Bova went 2-0 and moved to 11-3.

7|6.headline: Joshin Around starts three players who score nothing at all
7|6.body: George Kittle 0.00, Mike Evans 0.00, Jameson Williams 0.00 — three starters, no points, and a tight end position that finished the afternoon on zero with Dalton Schultz worth 22.3 more sitting behind it. Andrew got 49.82 from his quarterbacks and it bought him nothing. Mitch Blackwell's receivers went for 105.95 led by DeVonta Smith's 33.05, and i LOVE mendoza won by 48 in its best week since September. Both teams are 3-9 and this was, technically, the highlight of both their seasons.

8|1.headline: Tucker Kraft scores 36 and BoKnows723 hits 200 for the second time
8|1.body: 200.21, with 132.3 still sitting on the bench — Jake is now averaging a full extra team's worth of unused points every week and winning anyway. Tucker Kraft's 36.55 from the tight end slot was 22.2 clear of projection. Nick Merkel got 32.36 out of Breece Hall and 4.80 out of Bijan Robinson, which between them average out to a perfectly good afternoon and in practice meant an 84-point defeat. Nick went 0-2.

8|2.headline: eejacobs has the single best week anyone had all season
8|2.body: 65.8 points above par — the third-best showing against expectation anyone managed in 2025, and by some distance the best by a team that finished last. Erin did it with 11.7 points on his bench, having emptied the roster into the lineup. Jalen Hurts 27.36, Troy Franklin 26.4 from nowhere, Justin Herbert 25.28. Matt Bova started Marquise Brown for 0.00 with RJ Harvey worth 25.9 more, lost by 68, and went 0-2. This is the week eejacobs proved it could be done, and then finished 7-21 anyway.

8|3.headline: Chris Bova has 3.3 points on his bench and it is the whole story
8|3.body: Titsburg started essentially its entire useful roster — 3.3 points left on the bench, the emptiest bench anyone had all season. It produced 151.83 and 54.4 above par. Andrew Bova answered with 93.54, got 25.22 from Josh Allen and 6.62 from Dak Prescott, and fell to 3-11. Joshin Around has now lost eleven of fourteen and it is Week 8.

8|4.headline: James Cook 36.6, Christian McCaffrey 9.3, nobody in Paris cares
8|4.body: Nick's backfield produced 70.31 between two men pulling in opposite directions, and 163.05 was more than enough against a Mitch Blackwell side that managed 91.10 with two starters on zero. Quentin Johnston, benched in Week 1 and started ever since, contributed 0.00. Nabers in Paris is 12-2 and has won four straight; i LOVE mendoza went 0-2 for the eighth time.

8|5.headline: Two bad teams, 2.91 points, and a tight end who never showed up
8|5.body: Duane won 108.08 to 105.17 in a game neither side deserved — the second-closest finish of the season and comfortably the worst football involved in one. Jake Ferguson scored 0.00 for Enter the Maye-Trix, which should have ended it, except Jake Blackwell's entire quarterback contribution was Marcus Mariota's 11.32. Duane left 43.5 on the table and won by less than three. Neither team beat the median. Duane took a 1-1 out of it, Jake took an 0-2 and a fourth straight loss.

8|6.headline: Jared Hayes goes 32 above par and loses by six
8|6.body: Jonathan Taylor 37.9, a 72.95 backfield, 32.4 above par — this was a genuinely excellent week from SirWinsAlot, and Jerry Jeudy's 0.00 with Jalen Tolbert worth 12.7 more on the bench is the entire difference in a 5.74 game. Chris Merkel got 33.15 from Saquon Barkley and 4.08 from Baker Mayfield and squeaked home. Jared cleared the median for a 1-1, which is the fantasy football equivalent of a participation certificate.

9|1.headline: The closest game of the 2025 season, decided by 2.23 points
9|1.body: Joshin Around 147.87, Your Team is the PITTsMAN 145.64, and Andrew left 1.1 points on the table getting there — a near-perfect lineup in the one week he needed it. Chris Merkel started Rome Odunze for a 0.00 with Jalin Hyatt worth 4.4 more, which is twice the margin, and he will know that. The cruelty is the median: 150.39 was the second-highest of the season, so neither team cleared it. Andrew won the closest game of the year and went 1-1. Chris scored 145.64 and went 0-2.

9|2.headline: Matt Bova has his best week of the season and it is still a Penix story
9|2.body: 171.89 and 54.8 above par, one of the six best showings against expectation all season — Tee Higgins 33.35, Sam Darnold 29.2, Marvin Harrison 21.85. And Michael Penix sat on the bench worth 14.2 more than the Tua Tagovailoa in the QB slot. Five different weeks, five different wrong answers at the same position. Mitch Blackwell scored 152.91, 22.9 above par, cleared the median and lost by 19.

9|3.headline: Caleb Williams 40.2, Colston Loveland 33.05, and the 14-2 team goes down
9|3.body: Jared Hayes put 181.32 on Nabers in Paris with a tight end nobody had heard of in August going 24.9 above projection. SirWinsAlot got 61.4 from the quarterback slots and 46.4 from tight end, which is a lineup built entirely out of the wrong positions and it worked. Nick Bova's 168.44 was 15.5 above par, his backfield went for 88.75, and he lost — though he cleared the median for a 1-1, so the five-game winning streak dies quietly rather than expensively.

9|4.headline: Duane wins the game and loses the week
9|4.body: 134.61 beat 103.87 with room to spare, and the median was 150.39, so Enter the Maye-Trix banked exactly one win for a comfortable victory. Lamar Jackson's 25.56 led it. Erin Jacobs started Kayshon Boutte for 0.00 with Andrei Iosivas worth 17.0 more, got 21.0 from DeMario Douglas, and went 0-2. Both teams are 7-9 and this did nothing for either of them.

9|5.headline: Drake London scores 38 and Joe Flacco watches from the bench
9|5.body: Jake Bogardus won by 36 with 119.2 points unused, including a Joe Flacco worth 25.7 more than the Jordan Love he started in the SUPER_FLEX. Drake London's 38.3 covered every sin. Chris Bova had his worst week of the season — 126.54, 36.2 below par, with Jahmyr Gibbs managing 3.55 — and went 0-2 to end a four-game run. The two best teams in the league both had the same idea about how to spend Week 9 and only one of them got away with it.

9|6.headline: Brock Bowers scores 47.05 and ends a four-week losing streak on his own
9|6.body: The biggest single overperformance of the entire 2025 season: 47.05 against a 16.62 projection, 30.4 points clear, from a tight end. Nacua Matata scored 164.19 and 63.8 of the rest came from the receivers, which is to say Jake won this game with two positions and a prayer. Nick Merkel had 5.0 points on his bench — nothing left to give — started Evan Engram for a 0.00, and went 0-2. Both teams entered at 5-11. Only one of them is winning the championship in eight weeks' time.

10|1.headline: Jonathan Taylor scores 52.1 on his own and Matt scores 96 with a team
10|1.body: Taylor's 52.1 is the second-biggest individual afternoon anyone had in 2025, 29 points clear of projection, and it alone outscored Show Me Your Penix's entire receiving corps five times over — Matt's wideouts managed 16.18 between them. SirWinsAlot won by 101.44, the second-largest margin of the season, and finished 63.1 above par. Matt went 0-2. There is no joke here, just a scoreboard.

10|2.headline: De'Von Achane scores 40 and Nabers in Paris loses anyway
